project.name: Mini-DLSS
project.description: A from-scratch video frame interpolation pipeline inspired by NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation. Predicts the missing middle frame from two frames using Farneback optical flow and occlusion-aware bidirectional warping, evaluated with PSNR/SSIM. Phase 1 is a pure Python/OpenCV pipeline; Phase 2 adds CUDA kernels and a C++ desktop GUI application.

nodes.name: flow.h
nodes.summary: Declares the C++ Farneback optical-flow function for the native pipeline.

nodes.name: flow.cpp
nodes.summary: C++ port of optical flow: dense Farneback A->C returning a CV_32FC2 dx/dy field.

nodes.name: warp.h
nodes.summary: Declares the C++ flow-based frame warp function.

nodes.name: warp.cpp
nodes.summary: C++ port of frame warping: builds coordinate grids and inverse-warps with cv::remap bilinear interpolation.

nodes.name: blend.h
nodes.summary: Declares the occlusion mask and occlusion-aware blend functions for the C++ pipeline.

nodes.name: blend.cpp
nodes.summary: C++ port of occlusion handling: forward-backward consistency mask and mask-weighted blend of two warped frames.

nodes.name: video_io.h
nodes.summary: Declares VideoReader/VideoWriter wrappers and the VideoInfo struct over OpenCV videoio.

nodes.name: video_io.cpp
nodes.summary: OpenCV video I/O: reader that probes resolution/fps/frame-count and a writer with H.264->mp4v->XVID->MJPG codec fallback.

nodes.name: pipeline.cpp
nodes.summary: Native video-to-video pipeline: reads frames, interpolates each consecutive pair (CUDA or CPU path), and writes interpolated+real frames at 2x FPS with progress reporting and cancellation.

nodes.name: VideoReader
nodes.summary: OpenCV-backed reader that probes video metadata and yields frames.

nodes.name: VideoWriter
nodes.summary: OpenCV-backed writer with multi-codec fallback.

nodes.name: VideoInfo
nodes.summary: Struct holding width, height, fps, and frame count.

nodes.name: computeOpticalFlow
nodes.summary: C++ dense Farneback optical flow A->C returning a CV_32FC2 field.

nodes.name: warpFrame
nodes.summary: C++ inverse warp: builds coordinate grids and remaps the frame by t*flow with bilinear interpolation.

nodes.name: computeOcclusionMask
nodes.summary: C++ forward-backward consistency mask via cv::remap and exp(-error/threshold).

nodes.name: blendWithMask
nodes.summary: C++ occlusion-weighted blend: mask*warpedA + (1-mask)*warpedC.

nodes.name: Pipeline::run
nodes.summary: Opens input/output video, optionally inits CUDA, then interpolates every consecutive pair, writing interpolated+real frames at 2x FPS with progress and cancellation.

nodes.name: interpolatePair
nodes.summary: Interpolates one frame pair: bidirectional flow then occlusion-aware warp/blend, choosing the CUDA or CPU path.

nodes.name: VideoReader::open
nodes.summary: Opens a video and reads its resolution, fps, and frame count.

nodes.name: VideoWriter::open
nodes.summary: Opens an output video, trying codecs in preference order until one succeeds.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Top-level pipeline entry point. Wires together extract -> triplets -> baseline and flow interpolation, evaluates each triplet with PSNR/SSIM, and prints an averaged comparison of naive blend vs occlusion-aware flow interpolation.

nodes.name: extract.py
nodes.summary: Frame extraction stage: decodes an input video with OpenCV VideoCapture and writes every frame as a zero-padded PNG.

nodes.name: triplets.py
nodes.summary: Triplet builder: groups sequential frames into (A,B,C) sets where B is the ground-truth midpoint, with a configurable motion step, and persists the index as JSON.

nodes.name: baseline.py
nodes.summary: Naive baselines: simple and weighted pixel averaging of frames A and C, used as the motion-unaware reference to beat.

nodes.name: flow.py
nodes.summary: Optical flow stage: dense Farneback flow A->C plus an HSV visualization helper for inspecting motion fields.

nodes.name: warp.py
nodes.summary: Flow-based warping: remaps a frame along the flow field by an interpolation factor t and a simple two-frame midpoint interpolation built on it.

nodes.name: interpolate.py
nodes.summary: Phase-1 interpolation core: forward-backward occlusion mask plus occlusion-weighted bidirectional warp/blend to predict the middle frame.

nodes.name: evaluate.py
nodes.summary: Quality metrics implemented from scratch: PSNR from MSE and a windowed SSIM, plus a per-triplet evaluator returning both scores.

nodes.name: run_pipeline
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full mini-DLSS run: extract frames, build triplets, then per-triplet compute naive baseline and occlusion-aware flow interpolation, accumulate PSNR/SSIM, save samples, and print an averaged report.

nodes.name: extract_frames
nodes.summary: Decodes a video with cv2.VideoCapture and writes each frame as frame_NNNNN.png; returns the number of frames written.

nodes.name: create_triplets
nodes.summary: Builds (A,B,C) triplets from sorted PNG frames with a configurable step and writes the triplet index to JSON.

nodes.name: naive_blend
nodes.summary: Averages frames A and C 50/50 — the motion-unaware baseline.

nodes.name: weighted_blend
nodes.summary: Blends A and C with an adjustable alpha weight.

nodes.name: compute_optical_flow
nodes.summary: Computes dense Farneback optical flow A->C and returns an (H,W,2) float32 dx/dy field.

nodes.name: visualize_flow
nodes.summary: Encodes a flow field as an HSV image (hue=direction, value=magnitude) and saves it.

nodes.name: warp_frame
nodes.summary: Inverse-warps a frame along the flow field by factor t using cv2.remap with bilinear interpolation.

nodes.name: interpolate_with_flow
nodes.summary: Warps A forward and C backward to the midpoint and averages them (flow interpolation without occlusion handling).

nodes.name: compute_occlusion_mask
nodes.summary: Forward-backward flow consistency check: warps backward flow by forward flow, measures residual magnitude, and maps it to a soft [0,1] mask via exp(-error/threshold).

nodes.name: interpolate_with_occlusion
nodes.summary: Full Phase-1 prediction: bidirectional Farneback flow, occlusion mask, warp A & C to midpoint, and occlusion-weighted blend.

nodes.name: compute_psnr
nodes.summary: Computes PSNR from mean squared error using NumPy (returns inf when identical).

nodes.name: compute_ssim
nodes.summary: From-scratch SSIM using Gaussian-windowed luminance, contrast, and structure terms.

nodes.name: evaluate_triplet
nodes.summary: Loads the ground-truth frame and returns {psnr, ssim} for a predicted frame.

nodes.name: pipeline.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Pipeline class plus PipelineConfig/PipelineStatus and the progress-callback type.

nodes.name: cuda_backend.h
nodes.summary: Declares the CudaBackend class exposing GPU warp/blend/occlusion operations and device info.

nodes.name: cuda_backend.cpp
nodes.summary: Optional GPU backend: detects a CUDA device and marshals cv::Mat data into the extern-C kernel host wrappers; compiles to no-ops when HAS_CUDA is off.

nodes.name: app.h
nodes.summary: Declares the App controller and AppState enum: owns the CUDA backend, file paths, and worker-thread state.

nodes.name: app.cpp
nodes.summary: Application controller: launches the pipeline on a background std::thread, relays progress via a mutex-protected status, and supports cancellation.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Native executable entry point: parses args to run either a headless CLI conversion or the ImGui/GLFW desktop GUI (with a Windows WinMain variant).

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: GUI/CLI application controller: owns the CudaBackend, runs the pipeline on a worker thread, and exposes thread-safe state, status, and file-path setters.

nodes.name: Pipeline
nodes.summary: Runs the full video-to-video 2x interpolation; blocks until complete or cancelled and reports progress via callback.

nodes.name: PipelineConfig
nodes.summary: Config struct: input/output paths and the useCuda flag.

nodes.name: PipelineStatus
nodes.summary: Progress struct: current/total frames, fps, and a status message.

nodes.name: CudaBackend
nodes.summary: Optional GPU backend: detects a CUDA device and dispatches warp/blend/occlusion-mask kernels; degrades to no-ops without CUDA.

nodes.name: App::startProcessing
nodes.summary: Transitions to Processing state and spawns the worker thread.

nodes.name: App::workerThread
nodes.summary: Worker body: configures and runs the Pipeline, relaying progress and errors through the mutex-protected status.

nodes.name: App::init
nodes.summary: Initializes the CUDA backend and enables CUDA when a device is present.

nodes.name: runCli
nodes.summary: Headless conversion path: builds a PipelineConfig and runs the Pipeline with console progress.

nodes.name: runGui
nodes.summary: Boots GLFW + OpenGL3 + Dear ImGui, creates the App and Gui, and runs the render loop.

nodes.name: CudaBackend::warpFrame
nodes.summary: Copies frame+flow into the warp host wrapper, producing a GPU-warped frame (no-op without CUDA).

nodes.name: CudaBackend::blendFrames
nodes.summary: Dispatches the GPU blend host wrapper over two warped frames and a mask.

nodes.name: CudaBackend::computeOcclusionMask
nodes.summary: Dispatches the GPU occlusion-mask host wrapper over forward/backward flow.

nodes.name: CudaBackend::init
nodes.summary: Queries the CUDA device count/properties and records GPU name and VRAM.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Python dependencies: OpenCV, NumPy, scikit-image (reference SSIM), and PyCUDA (Phase-2 GPU integration).

layers.name: Python Reference Pipeline (Phase 1)
layers.description: The from-scratch Python/OpenCV implementation: extract frames, build triplets, baseline blend, optical flow, occlusion-aware warp/blend, and PSNR/SSIM evaluation. This is the readable reference the native app and CUDA kernels port.

layers.name: Native Pipeline Core (C++)
layers.description: The C++ port of the interpolation algorithms and video I/O — optical flow, warping, occlusion mask/blend, the video reader/writer, the pipeline orchestrator, and the CUDA backend bridge that marshals data to GPU kernels.

layers.name: Application Shell & UI
layers.description: The desktop application around the pipeline: CLI/GUI entry point, the threaded App controller, the Dear ImGui front-end, and the Windows system-tray integration.

layers.name: CUDA Acceleration (Phase 2)
layers.description: GPU kernels and their host wrappers: standalone teaching kernels (warp/blend/PSNR) and the app-integrated host wrappers (warp/blend/occlusion mask) callable from the C++ CudaBackend via extern-C.

layers.name: Build & Configuration
layers.description: Build and dependency definitions: the CMake build for the native app (OpenCV/CUDA/GLFW/ImGui), the Makefile for the standalone CUDA kernels, and the Python requirements.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Project documentation: the README overview and the CLAUDE.md repository guide.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the goal: predict the missing middle frame B from frames A and C using optical flow and occlusion-aware warping, then measure quality against ground truth.

tour.title: Pipeline Entry Point
tour.description: main.py orchestrates the whole Phase-1 run: extract -> triplets -> per-triplet baseline vs flow interpolation -> PSNR/SSIM report. Read it to see how the stages connect.

tour.title: Preparing Data: Frames & Triplets
tour.description: extract.py decodes the video into PNGs; triplets.py groups them into (A,B,C) sets where B is the ground-truth midpoint.

tour.title: The Baseline to Beat
tour.description: baseline.py just averages A and C. It has no motion awareness, so moving objects ghost — this is the reference the flow method must outperform.

tour.title: Estimating Motion: Optical Flow
tour.description: flow.py computes dense Farneback flow between frames and can visualize it as an HSV motion field.

tour.title: Moving Pixels: Warping
tour.description: warp.py remaps a frame along the flow to the midpoint. interpolate_with_flow warps A forward and C backward and averages them.

tour.title: Handling Occlusions (The Core Idea)
tour.description: interpolate.py adds the key trick: a forward-backward consistency mask down-weights pixels where the two flows disagree, then blends the two warps accordingly.

tour.title: Measuring Quality
tour.description: evaluate.py implements PSNR and SSIM from scratch to score predictions against ground truth.

tour.title: Porting to a Native App
tour.description: pipeline.cpp is the C++ video-to-video pipeline that interpolates every consecutive pair and writes a 2x-FPS output; main.cpp chooses between a headless CLI and the GUI.

tour.title: The C++ Algorithm Ports
tour.description: flow.cpp, warp.cpp, and blend.cpp mirror the Python stages using OpenCV in C++ — the CPU path of the native pipeline.

tour.title: GPU Acceleration with CUDA
tour.description: The CUDA kernels reimplement warp, blend, occlusion mask, and PSNR on the GPU. cuda_backend.cpp bridges OpenCV Mats to the extern-C host wrappers in app/cuda/.

tour.title: The Desktop GUI
tour.description: app.cpp runs the pipeline on a worker thread with thread-safe status; gui.cpp renders the Dear ImGui front-end with file pickers, controls, and a progress bar.

tour.title: Building It All
tour.description: CMakeLists.txt assembles the native app (fetching GLFW/ImGui, optional CUDA); the Makefile builds the standalone CUDA kernels into shared libraries.
